solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Tortured genius had to be feeling pain

indicators.note: something tortured is twisted out of shape, so these letters are wrenched into a new order

explanation.surface: A troubled genius had to suffer for their art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tortured' looks like a description of the genius, but it signals rearranging the letters of GENIUS HAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone in anguish is suffering acute mental or physical distress, a synonym for being in pain.

clue.text: A couple of bishops joining English priest in France

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop, so two of them give BB

explanation.surface: Two bishops team up with an English cleric working in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Abbé is the French title for a priest or abbot, used of clergy in France.

clue.text: Good old weapons making oblique impacts

parts.note: lances were spears carried by mounted knights, weapons of the past

explanation.surface: Old-fashioned arms produce blows that strike at an angle.
explanation.definitionFit: A glancing blow strikes at a slant and skids off, so such hits are oblique impacts.

clue.text: Set of beliefs is followed by millions

indicators.note: the first piece is followed by the second, so millions comes after is

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for million(s)

explanation.surface: A creed is something that millions of people follow.
explanation.definitionFit: An ism is any doctrine or ideology, a distinctive system of thought or belief.

clue.text: Decent hotel on East Street

parts.note: H is Hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A respectable hotel located on East Street.
explanation.definitionFit: A decent person is upright and truthful, which is what honest means.

clue.text: Democrat insisted on change — not one to toe the party line

definitions.text: not one to toe the party line

indicators.note: the word insisted is to be changed, its letters reordered

explanation.surface: A Democrat demands reform and so becomes a rebel within the party.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a party member insisting on reform; in fact 'change' scrambles the word insisted, and 'on' merely joins it to the Democrat's initial.
explanation.definitionFit: A dissident openly opposes official policy, so refuses to conform to the line laid down.

clue.text: Vessel to make discordant sound

definitions.meaning: a container such as a pot or crock for storing food
to grate harshly on the ear, as an off-key note does

explanation.definitionFit: A jar is a container, and to jar is to sound harshly or out of tune.

clue.text: Piece of meat, bit that's eaten at home

indicators.note: the bit swallows the next piece, so at home sits inside it

parts.note: a jot is a tiny amount, a bit
IN means at home, as in 'staying in'

explanation.surface: A cut of meat, a morsel of which gets eaten at home.
explanation.definitionFit: A joint is a large cut of meat for roasting, such as a leg of lamb.

clue.text: Reply in respect of something wrong in law

parts.note: RE means concerning or with regard to
a tort is a civil wrong in law

explanation.surface: A legal response concerning an alleged wrongdoing.
explanation.definitionFit: A retort is a sharp or witty answer, a type of reply.

clue.text: Servant without love — one who likes to row?

indicators.note: in its old sense of outside, so the servant goes round love

parts.note: a batman is an army officer's personal servant
O is zero, love in tennis scoring

explanation.surface: A lonely servant with no love life finds solace in rowing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but means 'outside'. The question mark flags a playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A boatman works or rows boats, so is someone who presumably enjoys rowing.

clue.text: Son isn't a good person

parts.note: AIN'T is the colloquial form of isn't

explanation.surface: A curt verdict: the boy is no angel.
explanation.definitionFit: A saint is someone of exceptional virtue, the model of a righteous individual.

clue.text: This person may appear on stage if the screens need moving

definitions.text: This person may appear on stage

indicators.note: the letters of if the screens must be moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: A stagehand might be seen by the audience if the scenery screens have to be shifted.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: the stagehand who shifts screens appears on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A scene-shifter is a stagehand who moves scenery, briefly visible on stage during changes.

clue.text: Scottish hooligan grabbing a university chair? Makes you sick!

indicators.note: the hooligan grabs and holds the other pieces inside

parts.note: a ned is Scottish slang for a young hoodlum
a seat, something to sit on

explanation.surface: A Glasgow thug seizing a professorship is enough to turn your stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chair' suggests a professorship, but here it just means SEAT. 'Makes you' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Nauseated means queasy, feeling as though one might vomit.

clue.text: Hairy man in the sauna

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the words the sauna

explanation.surface: A hirsute fellow sweating it out in the steam room.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Jacob's brother Esau is described as a hairy man.

clue.text: A head to give instruction? Not the head!

indicators.note: the first letter of the word for instructing is left off

parts.note: to teach is to instruct

explanation.surface: A headteacher with a teaching job, told they aren't the head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A head' means per person, as in 'five pounds a head'.
explanation.definitionFit: Charging so much a head means so much for every individual, i.e. per person apiece.

clue.text: Prisoner given shelter is happy

parts.note: a con is slang for a convict
a tent is a portable shelter

explanation.surface: A convict given a roof over their head is glad.
explanation.definitionFit: To be content is to be satisfied and at ease, a near synonym of pleased.

clue.text: I'm turning up in something with feathers or fur

indicators.note: the reversed piece goes inside the bird

parts.note: an erne is a sea eagle, a bird

indicators.note: in a down clue the letters of I'm are turned upward, read backwards

explanation.surface: Someone arriving dressed in plumage or a fur coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' works because this is a down clue, so I'm reads upward; 'something with feathers' is the crossword's favourite sea eagle.
explanation.definitionFit: Ermine is the white winter coat of the stoat, prized as a trimming on robes.

clue.text: Essence of report of army officer

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the officer's title is spoken

parts.note: a colonel is a senior army officer

explanation.surface: The gist of a senior officer's account.
explanation.definitionFit: The kernel of an argument is its core or central part, its essence.

clue.text: Theatre feeling bitter about performing again?

parts.note: rep is short for repertory theatre
resenting means feeling aggrieved over

explanation.surface: A theatre company is bitter about having to stage a revival.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a punning definition: read as RE-PRESENTING, putting on a show once more.
explanation.definitionFit: Split as re-presenting, the word means staging or presenting a show a second time.

clue.text: Quiet friend, as a friend may be

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quiet
an ally is a supporter or friend

explanation.surface: A shy companion, the way companions tend to be.
explanation.definitionFit: Pally is informal for friendly, the way a mate behaves.

clue.text: In conversation he would briefly care

indicators.note: in speech, so the contraction is spoken aloud

parts.note: he would shortened gives he'd

explanation.surface: Chatting, a man says he'd look after things.
explanation.definitionFit: To heed is to pay attention or take notice, a sense of the verb care.

clue.text: One group getting left in small place beset by water

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the group gets the next piece put inside it

parts.note: a set is a group

explanation.surface: A lone band stranded on a tiny spot surrounded by sea.
explanation.definitionFit: An islet is a little island, a patch of land ringed by water.

clue.text: Finally arrived? Or not to be seen?

definitions.meaning: as in the phrase '... to be seen', absent from view

explanation.walkthrough: The letters split differently for each sense: 'now here' versus the single word meaning in no place.
explanation.definitionFit: Split into two words it means present at last; as one word it means in no place at all.

clue.text: Witty person, one married to famous sportsman?

definitions.meaning: from ..., the wives and girlfriends of famous footballers

explanation.walkthrough: WAGs is a British tabloid term for footballers' wives and girlfriends.
explanation.definitionFit: A wag is a jokey wit, and a tabloid WAG is a star athlete's wife or girlfriend.

clue.text: See odd characters leaving Henley

indicators.note: the first, third and fifth letters of Henley go, leaving the even ones

explanation.surface: Watch the strange people leave Henley, the riverside regatta town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like a verb but is the noun: a bishop's diocese.
explanation.definitionFit: Ely, the cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, is the seat of a bishop, a diocese.

clue.text: Nominated member needing a short time to get into action

indicators.note: the pieces get inside the word for action

parts.note: a deed is an act or action
a leg is a limb, a member of the body
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: An elected representative needs a little time to spring into action.
explanation.definitionFit: To be delegated is to be appointed or deputed to act for others.
